      <content name="title"><span class="qt0">Vitiligo</span></content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p><span class="qt0">Vitiligo</span> causes white patches on your skin. It can also affect your eyes, mouth, and nose.  It occurs when the cells that give your skin its color are destroyed. No one knows what destroys them. It is more common in people with autoimmune diseases, and it might run in families. It usually starts before age 40.  </p><p>The white patches are more common where your skin is exposed to the sun. In some cases, the patches spread. <span class="qt0">Vitiligo</span> can cause your hair to gray early. If you have dark skin, you may lose color inside your mouth.  </p><p>Using sunscreen will help protect your skin, and cosmetics can cover up the patches. Treatments for <span class="qt0">vitiligo</span> include medicines, light therapy, and surgery. Not every treatment is right for everyone. Many have side effects. Some take a long time. Some do not always work.  </p><p>NIH: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases</p></content>

    <document rank="1" url="https://medlineplus.gov/skinpigmentationdisorders.html">
      <content name="title">Skin Pigmentation Disorders</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Hyperpigmentation</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Hypopigmentation</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Pigmentation means coloring. Skin pigmentation disorders affect the color of your skin. Your skin gets its color from a pigment called melanin. Special cells in the skin make melanin. When these cells become damaged or unhealthy, it affects melanin production. Some pigmentation disorders affect just patches of skin. Others affect your entire body. </p><p>If your body makes too much melanin, your skin gets darker. Pregnancy, Addison's disease, and sun exposure all can make your skin darker. If your body makes too little melanin, your skin gets lighter. <span class="qt0">Vitiligo</span> is a condition that causes patches of light skin. Albinism is a genetic condition affecting a person's skin. A person with albinism may have no color, lighter than normal skin color, or patchy missing skin color. Infections, blisters and burns can also cause lighter skin. </p></content>
